summary: A sound, cheap-to-kill test of whether the ~3.5 TB/s ceiling on the 67 MB streams is structural: a contiguous per-CTA region, one-thread bulk copies, and no split-K tail. The in-run pure-read kill gate makes even a loss decisive. Fix the incumbent numbers to master's (run 1602a4e947e64090), and expect m=32 to lag, because each CTA re-reads ALL of x from L2. It needs no cluster/DSMEM machinery, so it does not have to wait for the in-flight cluster checks.
justification: Shapes: pooler (4096x8192) and unpooler-full (8192x4096) are pure 67.1 MB weight streams at m<=32, with floors of 14.0-14.1 us. Master 1602a4e947e64090 incumbents (use these, not the restack's): pooler m=1/8/16 _bf16_splitk_kernel 19.0/19.3/19.5 us kernel (rows 19.00/19.14/19.85); pooler m=32 _bf16_swapab_kernel 20.5 (row 20.00); unpooler m=16 nvjet 64x16 18.5 (row 18.61); unpooler m=32 _bf16_swapab_kernel 18.9 (row 18.48). The hypothesis quotes the restack's 19.3 / 18.7 / 20.7 for unpooler m=16, unpooler m=32 and pooler m=32. That makes its unpooler M2 (<= 18.3 against '19.3') nearly a tie with master's 18.5. Restate M2 as pooler m=1 <= 18.5 and unpooler m=16 <= 18.0. Also, the restack did route pooler m<=16 to swap-AB (18.6/19.7/19.6), so 'the rows the restack does not cover' is loose wording, not a substantive error. Mechanism: the three claimed differences are real and untested together here. (c) No split-K is exact for both layers: 128 CTAs x 32 rows = 4096 and 128 x 64 = 8192, with K whole per CTA, so there is no ticket, workspace or tail. That directly removes the m-proportional cost that REWRITE_READ section 2 found in the gemv. (b) A one-thread bulk copy frees the consumer warps from issue. (a) Contiguity is the weakest of the three: HBM address hashing already spreads 512 B segments across channels, so expect at most a small row-buffer-locality gain. The in-run pure-read diagnostic is the right arbiter. Bytes in flight (~96 KB/SM x 128 ~ 12 MB) far exceed Little's-law needs (~5 MB at 4.8 TB/s x ~1 us), so depth is not the risk. Physics: practical large-stream read bandwidth on H200 is roughly 85-90% of 4.8 TB/s. With ~1-1.5 us of launch-to-first-byte ramp inside a ~16 us kernel, M3 (<= 16.5 us, 4.07 TB/s effective) is at the edge of physics; M2 (<= 18.5) is reachable. WEAKEST LINK: x traffic. Each CTA owns full K, so each CTA streams ALL of x through its ring: per CTA, m x 8192 x 2 B for pooler (512 KB at m=32, equal to its weight). Pooler's total L2->SM traffic is 67 MB of weight plus 128 x 512 KB = 67 MB of x at m=32 (twice the incumbent split-K=2's x traffic) and 33.5 MB at m=16. With L2->SM bandwidth in the ~5.5-7 TB/s class, m=32 pooler is likely L2-bound around ~19-24 us and m=16 marginal. m=1/8 (<= 16.8 MB of x) is where the mechanism is cleanly tested. The hypothesis already flags this and names multicast as stage 2, which is correct. A mechanical detail the change paragraph glosses: an x chunk [m x chunk-K] is NOT contiguous in global (row stride 16 KB pooler / 8 KB unpooler), so a 1-D bulk copy needs m separate row copies of 512 B / 256 B per slot, or a 2-D tensor map. Columns >= m in the slot are never written; that is harmless only because MMA columns are independent and never stored, so say so in the code, or zero-fill once at kernel start.
confounders: bf16-m32-swapab-wgmma-triton (landed): it is the incumbent on pooler m=32 and unpooler m=32. The new route runs before it, so there is no runtime interaction. Its tile is SPLIT_K=2, so it reads half the x traffic per CTA that this design does; an m=32 loss here is the x re-read, not the bulk stream. Read m=1/8 to judge the mechanism.

bf16-shape-gated-triton-winners-combo (landed): owns pooler m<=16 (_bf16_splitk_kernel). It is the incumbent and is bypassed by the gate, so it does not confound. Keep the new gate on its own bound constants so the combo's m<=16 bounds cannot widen the route by accident (LESSONS stack lesson).

sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (landed): the unpooler m=16 incumbent is its cuBLAS nvjet 64x16 path. cuBLAS rows vary between runs, so compare against 1602's 18.5 kernel and this run's own prepare-time cold-L2 side-by-side.

unpooler-full-m16-swapab-route (running, not landed): moves the same unpooler m=16 shape. Judge unpooler m=16 against both master's nvjet (18.5) and that harvest; the two do not stack, so whichever wins owns the shape.
interference: No companion is needed, and none would be readable sooner than the in-run diagnostics. The pure-read variant (same producer and ring, trivial consumers) already isolates the stream from MMA/x cost, and it is the kill gate. One cheap print-only addition makes the result fully attributable without a second check: a pure-read variant that issues the incumbent's access pattern (512 B row segments at a 16 KB stride from the ORIGINAL weight, same ring and bulk-copy issue). If contiguous and strided pure-read rates match, claim (a) is dead and any gain comes from (b)/(c). If contiguous is faster, the repack is the lever. The two in-flight cluster/DSMEM rewrites test cluster launch, mapa and barrier.cluster, none of which this kernel uses. cp.async.bulk with a .shared::cluster destination is valid under a non-cluster launch (an implicit 1-CTA cluster) and needs only sm_90. There is no reason to wait for them.
rules_flags: Repacking bf16 -> bf16 in prepare is lossless and allowed. Note that it adds ~134 MB of GPU memory, because the original pooler/unpooler weights must stay for the m>=33 cuBLAS and n=1024 slice paths.
Nothing derived from data is cached. Output via torch.empty and a shape-only gate are graph-safe. Diagnostics and syncs happen in prepare only.

mma.sync, ldmatrix and cp.async.bulk + mbarrier are plain sm_90. Still set TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=9.0a and -lineinfo, and print-and-sync after each self-check launch (LESSONS 2026-10-25). The first measurement must be an okc check.
open_questions: What cold pure-read rate does a 67 MB contiguous stream reach on the judge's H200? Below 3.8 TB/s means DEAD, as the hypothesis states. Remember that prepare event times undercounted the judge profile by 20-25% in the split-KV case (LESSONS), so a marginal 3.8-3.9 in prepare is likely 3.5 on the judge.

Is m=32 L2->SM bound by the full-x re-read? Compare full-kernel cold times at m=1/16/32 against pure-read. A widening gap with m confirms it and makes x multicast (cluster of 2-4 sharing x) the stage-2 lever.

Does one producer lane issuing 1 weight copy + m x-row copies per slot keep up at m=32 (33 bulk ops per 16 KB of weight)? If the full kernel lags pure-read even at m=8, split x issue across a second producer lane.
